Subject: Observed Dedicated capacity spike — next steps for renewal

Marissa,

Quick note from our side as we approach renewal: our Redwood Dedicated cluster for AtlasHealth has been consistently above the committed utilization from mid-November through December. We're seeing sustained higher throughput during peak windows (evening ET), and that pushed some inference jobs to queued/burst.

I pulled the high-level numbers and attached the Q4 usage snapshot — can we discuss what the right sizing looks like for the renewal? We're trying to avoid repeated overage charges but also need to avoid customer-impacting queuing. Prefer a short call this week to align on options (add GPUs vs. change autoscale/burst strategy vs. different model variants).

Thanks,
Emma Lewis

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>

Cc: Emma Lewis <emma@atlashealth.com>
Date: Wed, 14 Jan 2026 08:11:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Observed Dedicated capacity spike — next steps for renewal (sizing note)

Marissa / Logan / Emma — attaching a short technical summary of observed utilization and my recommendation. Key points up front:

- Current Dedicated pool: 8x A100-40GB (shared across two clusters, AtlasHealth has dedicated slice of 6 GPUs historically).
- Typical steady-state consumption: 60% of committed capacity (avg token/sec 18k across models) during daytime ET.
- Peak windows (17:00–22:00 ET): sustained 92–98% utilization for 3–5 hours on weekdays; we recorded 7 incidents of request queuing in Q4 correlated with batch jobs.
- KV-cache hit rate for atlas-prod: 42% on average (could improve with longer-lived requests / prefix caching).

Sizing recommendation (to meet 99.5% non-queued SLO and 95th latency similar to current):
- Option A (scale-up, conservative): add 4x A100-40GB (bring committed to 10 GPUs for AtlasHealth slice). Expected headroom: peak utilization ~65–72%.
- Option B (hybrid, cost-conscious): add 2x A100 + enable aggressive autoscale burst to shared pool during scheduled windows and tune KV caching. Expected peak utilization ~78–85% with occasional burst to shared capacity. Would need a policy for guaranteed tokens vs. best-effort.
- Option C (software-first): no GPU add, invest in model variant switching + quantized variants for high-volume routes — reduces cost but requires retraining/validations and can slightly increase latency on some endpoints.

Estimated impact on p50/p95 latency: Option A ~ neutral (same latency), Option B ~ +10–15% p95 during burst windows, Option C ~ +5–20% depending on model variant.

See attached short CSV and bullet notes. Let me know if you want a simulated monthly token-cost delta for each option; Logan, can you add numbers on the pricing side?

Cheers,
Dev Patel
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachments: AtlasHealth_sizing_note_20260114.txt (text)
From: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>

Cc: Emma Lewis <emma@atlashealth.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 15 Jan 2026 09:02:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Observed Dedicated capacity spike — pricing implications

Team / Emma — ran the numbers for the two most realistic options. High-level summary attached and pasted below. All numbers reflect committed monthly pricing plus expected on-demand burst in worst-case months.

- Option A (Add 4x A100 to committed slice -> 10 GPUs):
  * Incremental monthly commit: $48,000
  * Estimated blended per-token cost reduction: ~12% vs current because of reduced burst usage
  * 12-month committed delta (annualize): ~$576k

- Option B (Add 2x A100 + autoscale burst):
  * Incremental monthly commit: $25,800
  * Expected on-demand burst (worst months): additional $6k–$12k/month variable
  * 12-month committed delta: ~$309.6k (+ variable)

We also modeled a mid-year checkpoint (90-day utilization review with rightsizing credit if average utilization < 50% for three consecutive months). I included a proposed clause in the attached proposal spreadsheet (proposal_revised_20260115.xlsx).

Emma — if you'd like, Marissa and I can draft the contract language and suggested SLA targets (99.5% non-queued SLO) that align with Option A or B.

-Logan
Revenue Operations, Redwood Inference

Attachments: proposal_revised_20260115.xlsx

Thanks — this is exactly what I needed. A couple of quick items:

1) We prefer Option B initially (2 GPUs + burst) to avoid an immediate large capital commit. Please include the 90-day utilization checkpoint with a one-time right-sizing credit if AtlasHealth average utilization falls below 50% for three months after renewal.
2) Could you send a short addendum that lists expected p95 latency ranges under Option B and the operational escalation path if we see repeated queuing? Procurement will want that in the MSA appendix.
3) Let's hold the 30-minute call for Friday 14:00 ET so our engineering lead can join — Marissa, is that okay?

If you can get the addendum and updated proposal by EOD today, procurement can start legal review tomorrow.

Best,
Emma
Senior ML Ops, AtlasHealth
